BREAKING: The Democrats just got blindsided by Trump's newest executive order, and it's going to be a LOT harder for them to pursue their endless witch hunt against this admin!

Before the Democrats ever took power, they already promised a wave of investigations into the Trump administration.

However, President Trump just slammed the door.

On Friday, he signed an executive order aimed at federal contractors. 

Here's what it does:

-If Congress asks a contractor for info about its work with the government, the contractor has to tell the White House.

-If the White House says that info is private, the contractor has to keep it private.

-Contractors have to follow the White House's lead, not Congress's.

-Subcontractors have to follow the same rules.

Why does this matter? The White House says some in Congress were going around the normal process to dig up confidential files.

The order says "certain congressional leaders have threatened to intrude on these Executive prerogatives by seeking confidential executive branch information from agencies and harassing private companies that contract with the Federal Government."

That back door is now closed.

Trump saw the next round of investigations coming and got there first.

BIG WIN!!!!

posts.text:
In a ruthless 2019 parody sketch, a deadpan George Lucas impersonator watches the final trailer for Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker roasting Disney's sequel trilogy with brutal sarcasm while celebrating the fact that he cashed out and isn't to blame for any of it.

From the very first frame, "Lucas" cheers every time the Lucasfilm logo appears ("another check for daddy") before tearing into Rey's effortless mastery of the Force, comparing her trajectory to Luke Skywalker losing his hand and Han Solo getting frozen in carbonite at the end of The Empire Strikes Back.

Nothing survives the commentary he mocks the new droid D-O as a literal hairdryer on wheels, ridicules Star Destroyers rising out of the ocean and space horses charging across hulls, jokes that the film makes Attack of the Clones look like Citizen Kane, and delivers a deadpan "spoiler" for the ending: Star Wars officially dies.

Wrapping up with a satirical breakdown of Joseph Campbell's classic Hero's Journey and self-deprecating digs at his own prequel trilogy being "tone poems" free of logic or traditional acting the sketch captures the peak of internet backlash during the sequel era
